subject.title: fix(agents): protect provider auth exchange output by sensitivity, not input marker

question: Should all non-empty provider auth exchange outputs be treated as secret unless `isNonSecretApiKeyMarker` explicitly classifies them as public?
rationale: The implementation, dependency contracts, complete egress path, live proof, and current merge result support this fail-safe rule, but it is the permanent shared classification policy for all provider plugins and the affected files are security-owned.

options.title: Approve secret-by-default outputs
options.body: Land this patch and require every intentionally public provider output marker to be declared in the central marker contract.

options.title: Require typed sensitivity metadata
options.body: Pause and redesign `prepareRuntimeAuth` so each output explicitly declares whether it is sensitive.

options.title: Limit the fix to Mantle
options.body: Special-case the known provider, preserving the weaker shared rule and recurrence risk for future exchanges.

recommendation.title: Approve secret-by-default outputs
recommendation.body: Land this patch and require every intentionally public provider output marker to be declared in the central marker contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and recently hardened the shared sentinel-egress security model whose classification rule changes here.
